description:
Create a new phone verification session. Returns deep_link, qr_code (base64 PNG), and qr_text (UTF-8 text QR for terminal display). Sessions provide a hosted verification flow with callbacks.

Agent usage: After creating a session, pass the response's `deep_link` to render_auth_link so the user can open or scan it. Never hand `qr_text` to a link renderer — it is that link already rendered as QR art. Print it verbatim inside a fenced code block only when a real terminal needs the QR. On sms the person texts a short code from the number being proven, as in SMS login: `deep_link` is an `sms:` link to our default number with the message pre-filled, so render it the same way, and also show `sms_message` (what they send) with the numbers in `sms_dids` (one per region, each with its own QR), because a person reading on a computer texts from their phone. They get no reply SMS. An SMS proof can still be revoked about a minute after the session completes, if the delayed spoof check finds the sender was not a real mobile line, so before relying on it check it with validate_proof. Then use wait_for_session to poll until the session reaches a terminal state (verified, failed, or expired).

The user does not see tool results — most clients fold them away, render_auth_link's output included. Before you wait or poll, put what the user must act on into your own reply text: the link itself (not a sentence announcing it), the SMS text and number, or a note to check their inbox.

ACCESS: needs a Proof account. Set PROOF_API_KEY and restart this server, then call this tool again. start_login does NOT open this tool.

channel.description: How the person proves the number: telegram or whatsapp (the bot reads it from their account) or sms (they text a short code from it). No phone number is sent

client_metadata.description: Your own key-value data, stored with the session

action.description: Picks the bot's wording: log in, 2FA, account recovery, or plain verification (the default)

profile_id.description: Sub-account whose name and templates the bot uses; omitted: the key's sub-account, else the primary

name: create_session

channel.description: How the person proves the number: `telegram` or `whatsapp` (the bot reads the number from their account), or `sms` (they text a short code from the number to one of ours).

deep_link.description: Opens the messenger (`https://t.me/…`, `https://wa.me/…`) or the messaging app (`sms:<number>?body=…`) with what the person sends

instructions.description: One line telling the person what to do

qr_text.description: UTF-8 text QR for `deep_link`, for terminal/agent rendering

sms_code.description: The short code the person texts (`sms` only)

sms_dids.description: Every number an `sms` session's code can be texted to, one per configured region (a region with no number is absent), each with its own QR code. `deep_link` uses the default region's number; the request comes from your server, so nothing in it says where the person is.

sms_message.description: The message to send, as pre-filled in the links (`sms` only)
